page_intro: COSI Lab studies hip and knee surgery using clinical data, imaging, biomechanical modeling, and surgical robotics. We welcome students, orthopaedic trainees, and researchers interested in this work.
apply_text: Review our current research, then use the application form to tell us about your background and the work you are interested in.
level1_desc: Contribute methods for learning from movement, video, and wearable sensors. Relevant interests include foundational model development, evaluation across patients and devices, and testing whether predictions remain useful in independent clinical datasets.
level2_desc: Apply mechanics, computation, or experimental design to tendon repair models and questions in implant design. Relevant work examines load sharing, mechanical failure, and how well simulations agree with experimental measurements.
level3_desc: Investigate clinical presentation and imaging in abductor tears and recovery after surgery. Relevant contributions include evidence review, clinical data analysis, and assessment of pain, walking, and other functional outcomes.
level4_desc: Bring clinical questions about repair selection, surgical constructs, complications, or recovery. Research interests may include interpreting imaging and operative findings, comparing outcomes, and assessing how study results could inform patient care.
level5_desc: Develop research in movement modeling, biomechanics, or clinical data analysis. Areas of interest include experimental validation, bias in observational studies, and testing the performance of prediction models in independent patient populations.
